# #451 Latinamerika-special

**Feed**: market-makers  
**Published**: 2026-10-08  
**Market Sentiment**: Positive

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

The Market Makers hosts covered Swedish IPOs and one acquisition company before turning to Latin America. Prisjakt's First North IPO was discussed as a contrarian idea. The Prisjakt case rests on a low valuation of about 5x EBITDA and an optional damages claim against Google, after Pricerunner won a similar ruling. One host pitched Tången, which he owns, as an acquirer trading cheaply against Idun and Carnell. The hosts called the drop in Chefello after its trading update an overreaction, and both bought more shares. The Latin America section looked at the Brazilian election, where Bolsonaro led round one with 47% to Lula's 45%. Inter & Co was a watch idea on that outcome, and Fabian pitched Liberty Latin America as a sum-of-the-parts buy at about a 12% free cash flow yield.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 LILAK — Liberty Latin America | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

Sum-of-the-parts case: stable duopolies, ~12% FCF yield ex Puerto Rico, Malone buying, buybacks, cable unit option. Fabian intends to buy at the open.

#### Reasoning

Fabian (host) argues the debt sits in separate subsidiaries without cross-guarantees, so Puerto Rico (~$3B debt, burning cash) can't sink the parent. Triggers he lists: lenders taking over Puerto Rico; operating profit recovery (Jamaica after the hurricane, cost cuts), where +10% operating profit means ~+50% FCF; $140M of buybacks left plus ~$90M from the Peru stake sale; a re-rating of Liberty Networks. Fair value ~$12-13 vs ~$8.

#### Sell Triggers

- if operating profit/revenue fails to grow amid price pressure
- if refinancing (~end-2028) occurs at much higher rates
- if Puerto Rico liabilities spill over to parent
- if management makes further poor acquisitions
- major hurricane damage

> *"Det här är ett halv-songs-case. Du köper en stabil duopol. Och kursen idag prisar in dagens klassaflöde men inte mycket mer."*

---

### 🟢 CHEF — Chefello | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Hosts say the 12-14% drop after the trading update is an overreaction; EV/EBIT ~9 and 5-10% dividend yield expected. Both hosts bought more today.

#### Reasoning

Active customers fell 9% because of a one-off Q3 2025 cohort (Norwegian reactivation campaign and SAS campaign) that made the comparison tough. The host had expected -4%. The update was somewhat weaker even after adjusting for that, but he says the story is intact. The key unknown is marketing spend; the CEO says the focus is ROI, not volume. The host bought; the co-host bought but may sell during the day.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Q3 report shows marketing spend sharply up vs last year
- if active customer decline continues beyond comparison effects
- if dividend capacity weakens

> *"Men jag tror att det är lite överreaktion på det här. Och tycker att aktien ser väldigt billig ut nu helt enkelt."*

---

### 🟠 INTR — Inter & Co | **WATCH** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Brazilian digital bank, up 20%+ on the election. A possible play on a Bolsonaro win and lower rates later. Host hasn't bought.

#### Reasoning

45M customers (about 1/5 of Brazilian bank accounts) and 30%+ growth in Q2. A business-friendly Bolsonaro government could cut spending and eventually bring rates down from ~15%. Not very expensive, but the high Brazilian rate is a concern. The final round is on 25 October.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Lula wins the 25 Oct runoff
- if Brazilian policy rate stays ~15% or rises

> *"Så det kan vara ett intressant case att kika in. Jag har dock inte köpt någonting själv än, men jag tycker att det här känns rätt spännande faktiskt."*

---
